subject: Action plan kickoff: initial MAP draft and timeline options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Action plan kickoff: initial MAP draft and timeline options

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the first-pass Mutual Action Plan (attached) so we can align on milestones, owners, and a target close. Please read through and either: (A) confirm stakeholders + preferred timeline, or (B) mark changes and I’ll update the doc.

High-level summary from discovery:
- Primary use case: inference at scale for analytics assistant (low-latency, batch embeddings)
- Key constraints: SOC2 evidence, data residency in us-east, procurement window in mid-Jan
- Success metric: P50 latency < 200ms for 512-token prompts; pilot within 6 weeks

Attached: RDW_MAP_draft_v1.pdf (MAP v1 — milestones, owners, dependencies)

Two timeline options (pick one):
1) Aggressive — 6 week path (Kickoff week of 12/6, Pilot by 1/15, Production-ready by 2/12)
   - Milestones: Kickoff, Security review, Procurement PO, Pilot run, Production cutover
   - Risks: Procurement approval could slip; SOC2 artifact delivery required early
2) Standard — 10 week path (Kickoff week of 12/13, Pilot by 2/1, Prod by 3/1)
   - Milestones: same as above, more breathing room for procurement & infra changes

Mapping of responsibilities (in MAP):
- Acme: security questionnaire completion, procurement PO, stakeholder availability for pilot
- Redwood: environment setup, SOC2 evidence packaging, pilot support, onboarding workshop

Dependencies called out in the MAP:
- SOC2 evidence (security/compliance) — Acme requires a specific artifact list (we asked for the list on the call)
- Procurement lead time — if PO not issued by 1/6, aggressive timeline at risk
Asks (two quick asks):
1) Please confirm the primary stakeholders on your side who should appear on the MAP (name + role + email).
2) Which timeline option do you prefer (Aggressive / Standard) and any hard constraints on procurement?

Next steps after you reply: I’ll incorporate stakeholder list, lock a kickoff date, and send an updated MAP and calendar invite.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake

- Rajiv Patel — Security Lead (rajiv.patel@acmeanalytics.com)
- Emily Chen — Procurement Manager (procurement@acmeanalytics.com)

Procurement note: Emily flagged that our standard PO cycle will likely push any spend approval to the week of 1/10. If we need PO earlier for the aggressive timeline we’ll have to use a temporary contract or expedite legal. I’ll loop Emily and she can advise.

Security/compliance: Rajiv said he needs a SOC2 artifact list (control mapping + logs retention) before we start environment provisioning. Is that something Redwood can provide by 12/10?

Timeline preference: We’d prefer the Standard 10-week option unless Redwood can guarantee the SOC2 artifacts and a procurement workaround for the aggressive timeline.

Next: Emily — can you confirm procurement timeline and share any legal/vendor redline owners?

Thanks — Sarah
